correctness.rationale: The LCF graph is fixed by explicit 18-vertex/27-edge data. Two independent perfect-matching enumerations return the same 42 facets; independent matching completion checks all 35,368 matchings, yielding 15,820 extendible subsets including empty. The reproducible Morse matching has 7,901 pairs on 15,819 nonempty faces and is acyclic by exhaustive directed topological sorting of 78,921 incidences. Signed gradient-path boundary reduction gives an explicit 5-by-10 integer differential with a 5-by-5 minor of determinant -1 and a zero 10-by-1 next differential. It follows via Hurewicz and homological Whitehead, not merely from finite-field ranks, that the complex is a wedge of five 3-spheres and one 4-sphere. Exact certificate, Python replay and independent mod-two simplicial checks are included. Computational scope is finite and complete.

value.rationale: The standard Pappus Levi graph is a canonical cubic symmetric nonplanar incidence graph. Perfect-matching extendibility is an established natural simplicial construction, and its complete integral homotopy type is mathematically distinct from the same graph’s known ordinary matching-complex type. The mixed-dimensional wedge is a precise, reusable finite benchmark for the distinction between matching and perfect-matching topology. It is not merely a numerical face count, arbitrary parameter slice or consequence of the published ordinary-complex theorem. No unsupported family-wide consequence is claimed.
